milestones.title: A room and a clear question
milestones.why: Choose the place your rover will measure and the one visual distinction your model will learn.

milestones.title: A chassis with measured fits
milestones.why: Build serviceable mounts and a rolling structure whose geometry you can explain.

milestones.title: A model whose mistakes you understand
milestones.why: Train on your own images and preserve an honest comparison before adding robot context.

milestones.title: Wheels that follow requests and stop
milestones.why: Give later navigation a measured, bounded way to move the rover.

milestones.title: Measurements in the right coordinates
milestones.why: Make camera, lidar and wheel observations agree about units, time and position.

milestones.title: A room map you can check
milestones.why: Compare the map with physical dimensions and save the evidence needed to rebuild it.

milestones.title: A short trip with dependable stopping
milestones.why: Demonstrate one supervised route and the conditions under which the rover should refuse it.

milestones.title: Five real observations with a place and time
milestones.why: Connect your model and measured room without inventing the toy’s location.

sessions.title: Choose the room and the toy
sessions.why: One bounded room and one distinctive object make the first robot experiment specific enough to test.
needs: Computer, camera and tape measure
One clear area on a single floor; stair access will be physically blocked for powered tests
actions: Create home-rover with notes, cad, data and runs folders.
Photograph and sketch the test area; mark three measured spans and their exact endpoints.
Write the one-sentence present/absent question for your chosen toy.
sessions.finish: Your notes identify the room, measurement endpoints and target object.
sessions.artifact: notes/room-reference.md, a room photograph and the target sentence
sessions.restart: Open the room sketch and point to one measured span in the real room.
sessions.diagnostic: If choosing the room stalls you, use one clear section with three accessible reference spans and record that boundary.
sessions.shortAction: Choose the object and write its one-sentence label rule.

reference.label: Why capture sessions must stay separate

sessions.uncertainty: The first experiment measures one bounded area; whole-house coverage remains a later question.

sessions.title: Capture your first twenty examples
sessions.why: These are the first images your own model will learn from while the rover is still being built.
needs: The selected toy and an existing camera
home-rover/data; ordinary image files with people and private material kept out of frame
actions: Create data/train/A/present and data/train/A/absent.
Alternate ten present and ten absent photographs with varied viewpoints and backgrounds.
Open the files and check their labels; record the camera and capture conditions.
sessions.finish: Twenty distinct images open correctly and are in their matching session and label folders.
sessions.artifact: data/train/A with ten images per class and a capture note
sessions.restart: Open one present and one absent image from session A and check their folder labels.
sessions.diagnostic: If the images look almost identical, change viewpoint and placement; do not duplicate files to reach twenty.
sessions.shortAction: Capture and label one varied present/absent pair, then note the remaining count.

reference.label: Keep related images in one split

sessions.uncertainty: Session A alone cannot train and evaluate the complete experiment; later capture sessions provide independent comparisons.

sessions.title: Measure one physical interface
sessions.why: A measured bolt or pin gives your printed fit experiment a real mating part.
needs: Calipers and one actual M3 through-bolt or smooth pin
The fit-log template from this session
actions: Clean and zero the caliper jaws.
Measure the part in more than one direction and record units and method.
Save the first fit-log entry and name the coupon you will print next.
sessions.finish: The log identifies a real measured part and the next small print.
sessions.artifact: The first row of your fit log and the labelled mating part
sessions.restart: Find the same part and repeat one recorded dimension.
sessions.diagnostic: If readings vary, check zero and jaw contact and use light consistent pressure before changing the design.
sessions.shortAction: Zero the calipers and record one repeated measurement.
sessions.uncertainty: A nominal M3 label or caliper display resolution does not establish a printed hole’s fit.

sessions.title: Save a repeatable X1 Carbon recipe
sessions.why: Holding the print process steady lets you tell whether a geometry change improved the fit.
needs: Bambu Studio, X1 Carbon and PLA already known to print well
The actual installed nozzle and build plate; the coupon geometry assumes a 0.4 mm nozzle
actions: Select the actual printer, nozzle, plate and filament profile.
Save the chapter’s baseline process and arranged 3MF; record compensation settings.
Add material and process details to the fit log before printing.
sessions.finish: A saved 3MF and process record identify the actual configuration used for the coupon.
sessions.artifact: X1C-survey-PLA-baseline, the coupon 3MF and fit-log process fields
sessions.restart: Open the saved 3MF and confirm its nozzle, plate and material match the printer.
sessions.diagnostic: If the selected profile differs from your installed hardware, correct that mismatch before comparing dimensions.
sessions.shortAction: Record the installed nozzle, plate and filament and save the named process copy.
sessions.uncertainty: The baseline makes comparison repeatable; your own coupon measurements establish the local fit.

sessions.title: Print and measure a fitting pair
sessions.minutes: About 30 minutes active work, plus printing
sessions.why: A small successful fit can be transferred into a serviceable mount before you print the whole chassis.
needs: Saved X1C baseline, clearance strip, actual M3 screw and calipers
Let prints cool before comparing fits; use light finger pressure
actions: Print the clearance strip with the unchanged baseline and label its slots.
Try the same screw in each slot without cutting threads; repeat the measurements.
When a round fit matters, print and check the round coupon and pin in their stated orientations.
sessions.finish: You can show a fitting pair with measured dimensions, material, orientation and a repeat check.
sessions.artifact: A labelled coupon, its mating part and completed fit-log rows
sessions.restart: Find your first passing pair and verify the same part still fits with light pressure.
sessions.diagnostic: If none fit, inspect a first-layer lip and repeat one measurement before changing one clearance parameter.
sessions.shortAction: Label the cooled strip and record the fit in one slot.

reference.label: Design for printed fits and orientation

sessions.uncertainty: This result applies to the measured feature, orientation and process; different geometry needs another small check.

sessions.title: Collect the independent image sessions
sessions.minutes: 45–60 minutes per visit; several visits may help
sessions.why: Independent capture sessions let us test whether the model learned something useful beyond one photographic setup.
needs: Session A, the same target toy and a camera
A fixed label rule; whole sessions assigned before any fitting
actions: Collect sessions A–H with varied conditions and both labels in each session.
Assign A–D to training, E–F to validation and G–H to the reserved final test.
Check ambiguous labels and record the next missing session if collection needs another visit.
sessions.finish: Every declared session contains both labels and each whole session belongs to exactly one split.
sessions.artifact: The A–H image folders, capture notes and written split assignment
sessions.restart: Open the capture log and identify the next missing session without renaming an existing one.
sessions.diagnostic: If a shortcut cue appears, inspect whether hands or backgrounds predict the label; collect a genuinely varied session.
sessions.shortAction: Collect one small varied present/absent set for the next named session and record what remains.
sessions.uncertainty: The initial 160-image target exercises the pipeline; it does not promise useful recognition throughout the house.

sessions.title: Make the training pipeline run
sessions.minutes: One or more 45–60 minute setup blocks
sessions.why: A checked CPU environment lets you inspect your real inputs before hardware or GPU setup adds more variables.
needs: Windows 11, Python 3.12 and PowerShell in home-rover
Extract the chapter’s training ZIP directly beside data; use the declared session folders
actions: Create the documented CPU environment and run the supplied synthetic smoke check.
Generate and validate data/manifest.csv from your declared sessions.
Make the training-input contact sheet and inspect the actual 64 × 64 images.
sessions.finish: The synthetic check passes, the manifest validates, and the target is inspectable in the resized training images.
sessions.artifact: Environment versions, data/manifest.csv and reports/train-inputs.png
sessions.restart: Open the saved input sheet and rerun the small import or manifest check that last passed.
sessions.diagnostic: Fix the first named installation, file or session error; preserve capture groups instead of changing IDs to silence it.
sessions.shortAction: Extract the starter to home-rover and confirm learn.py sits beside data.
sessions.uncertainty: The supplied pipeline was checked on Linux CPU; your Windows execution and any later GPU environment require their own check.

sessions.title: Train a baseline and inspect its mistakes
sessions.why: A simple trained comparison tells you whether the later CNN earns its extra complexity.
needs: Passing training environment and validated manifest
Keep preprocessing fitted on training data only; leave the reserved test unopened
actions: Run the supplied baseline training command in a new run directory.
Create the detailed validation report and contact sheet.
Explain one error or boundary example and locate the training-only scaler fit.
sessions.finish: The baseline and its validation evidence are saved, and you can explain what data fitted its preprocessing.
sessions.artifact: runs/baseline, validation-details.json and the validation image sheet
sessions.restart: Open the saved validation sheet and inspect one image with its label and prediction.
sessions.diagnostic: If the score is surprising, inspect the exact resized image and session split before changing the model.
sessions.shortAction: Read one confusion-matrix row and open one corresponding validation image.

reference.label: Read the mistakes behind the score

sessions.uncertainty: A small validation result is evidence about these sessions, not established household accuracy.

sessions.title: Train the CNN and compare the evidence
sessions.why: Learning small image filters lets you test a different representation against the same baseline.
needs: The unchanged dataset, passing environment and saved baseline
Use validation for checkpoint selection; keep final test data reserved
actions: Train the supplied small CNN with the declared seed and a new output directory.
Trace gradient reset, backpropagation and optimizer update in learn.py.
Inspect reload checks, history and validation mistakes beside the baseline’s results.
sessions.finish: The neural checkpoint reloads, both validation reports are saved, and you can explain one parameter update.
sessions.artifact: runs/cnn-7, history.csv, run.json and the neural validation sheet
sessions.restart: Open run.json and the validation sheet to recover the exact model and data version.
sessions.diagnostic: If the CNN loses, compare its resized inputs and errors with the baseline before adding layers.
sessions.shortAction: Find make_cnn and identify one Conv2d weight and the three optimizer-update steps.
sessions.uncertainty: The neural model may lose to the baseline; that is a legitimate comparison rather than a failed course checkpoint.

sessions.title: Freeze the comparison and test it once
sessions.why: A reserved evaluation records what survived a new capture after your model choices were fixed.
needs: Both saved runs and their validation reports
Write the frozen model, preprocessing and threshold choices before opening final test reports
actions: Record the fixed comparison and evaluate both runs on the reserved test split.
Inspect per-session results and the permitted test error sheets.
Predict one real image and write the result, limitation and next useful data collection.
sessions.finish: Both frozen reports and reload evidence exist, with an explanation of a failure or still-untested condition.
sessions.artifact: Final test reports, saved model identifiers and a three-sentence experiment conclusion
sessions.restart: Read the frozen-comparison note before touching the test data or changing code.
sessions.diagnostic: If test errors suggest a redesign, keep the reports and reserve fresh sessions for the next final evaluation.
sessions.shortAction: Write the comparison choices and threshold using the validation evidence already saved.
sessions.uncertainty: Once test errors guide changes, those sessions become development evidence; a new claim needs a fresh final test.

sessions.title: Place the real components in Fusion
sessions.why: An editable assembly catches collisions, unreachable fasteners and unstable packaging before a full print.
needs: Fusion in millimetres, measured component drawings and the passing fit coupon
Read the chapter’s selected motor, bracket, wheel and third-contact details; verify delivered revisions and include cable/tool space
actions: Create separate deck, drive, support and electronics components with the stated body-frame convention.
Set the measured deck height and wheel geometry, then place simple component envelopes.
Check the support triangle, wheel clearances, scan view and reachable disconnect and fasteners.
sessions.finish: The layout shows a shared axle line, three support contacts, clear cables and removable components.
sessions.artifact: The native Fusion assembly and a labelled front/side-view screenshot
sessions.restart: Open the side view and verify that the wheels reach the floor and the deck clears it.
sessions.diagnostic: If parts collide, move their simple envelopes and verify actual drawing dimensions before adding detail.
sessions.shortAction: Create the named components and place one measured motor envelope.
sessions.uncertainty: The initial deck dimensions are a packaging trial; the course does not supply a physically validated complete chassis design.

sessions.title: Make one bracket mount fit
sessions.minutes: About 45–60 minutes active work, plus printing
sessions.why: One removable, well-located bracket establishes the mounting pattern the full deck will reuse.
needs: The Fusion layout and a delivered bracket with its current drawing
Passing coupon clearance, through-bolts, washers and nuts
actions: Model only the deck region under one bracket with named dimensions and measured hole spacing.
Print in the intended deck orientation and test both fastener and tool access.
Fix the deck and use the appropriate rigid joint to preserve the bracket position in CAD.
sessions.finish: The bracket fits without forcing, remains located under a gentle hand load and can be removed.
sessions.artifact: Native Fusion mount design, slicer project and photograph of the fitted bracket
sessions.restart: Open the mount design and place the same bracket on the printed coupon.
sessions.diagnostic: If it binds, compare measured hole spacing and clearance separately; avoid scaling the whole assembly.
sessions.shortAction: Measure the delivered bracket’s selected hole spacing and enter one named parameter.
sessions.uncertainty: The local mounting check establishes fit and serviceability; it does not certify the full deck’s load capacity.

sessions.title: Assemble a chassis that rolls freely
sessions.why: A mechanically sound, accessible rover gives the motor and sensor experiments a stable base.
needs: Passing mounting coupon, full deck and measured unpowered components, including the selected third contact
Use correct screw engagement and wheel collets; keep representative masses secured
actions: Print and assemble the deck only after the local mount passes.
Set the third contact height and roll the unpowered chassis over clean hardwood.
Check wheel/caster clearance, mount stiffness, fastener access and the physical disconnect.
sessions.finish: The loaded layout sits on three contacts, retains its parts and rolls without visible binding.
sessions.artifact: Assembly photographs, measured footprint, loaded radius estimate and wheel-centre separation
sessions.restart: With power disconnected, repeat the gentle hand-roll and clearance check.
sessions.diagnostic: If a wheel rubs or a mount moves, repair that physical interface before adding motor power.
sessions.shortAction: Check one wheel’s full rotation and record any rubbing or wobble with power disconnected.
sessions.uncertainty: A roll check supports the prototype layout; it is not a rated payload or endurance test.

sessions.title: Trace and check the motor power path
sessions.why: A checked power path lets the first wheel experiment begin with known polarity and a reachable stop.
needs: Read the reference-electronics and purchase-gate context; use exact board and pack documentation
Battery disconnected for wiring and continuity; motor outputs disconnected for first controller power
Correct fuse, DC-rated disconnect, secured wiring and a separate supported PC supply
actions: Draw the positive fuse/disconnect path and direct negative return using the real board labels.
Check the unpowered harness for continuity and unintended shorts.
Measure disconnected-pack polarity and charged voltage in DC voltage mode; record limits before connecting the controller.
sessions.finish: You can trace both conductors, identify the fuse/disconnect and show measured polarity before any motor turns.
sessions.artifact: Labelled wiring diagram, harness inspection and pack-voltage record
sessions.restart: Leave the pack disconnected and trace the diagram against the labelled harness.
sessions.diagnostic: If a reading is unclear, isolate the unpowered harness and check the meter’s sockets and mode before proceeding.
sessions.shortAction: With power disconnected, draw and label the battery-positive to controller-positive path.
sessions.uncertainty: Wire protection, voltage settings and regeneration behavior depend on your actual pack and controller; documentation is not a completed bench check.

sessions.title: Read and turn one wheel, then the other
sessions.why: Verified direction and encoder counts connect software requests to measurable physical motion.
needs: Checked power path, Windows Motion Studio and exact motor/controller pinouts
Power disconnected while wiring; chassis secured with wheels suspended
Encoder power comes from the documented low-voltage supply, not motor outputs
actions: Wire one motor and encoder from the verified pinout and record controller/firmware identity.
At zero command, hand-turn one marked revolution and inspect the count convention.
Use a brief low-duty request, verify direction/sign and return to zero; repeat separately for the other wheel.
sessions.finish: Each positive command and count agrees with forward motion, channels stay distinct and zero halts both wheels.
sessions.artifact: The completed direction/count log and saved controller settings
sessions.restart: With output commands inhibited, hand-turn one marked wheel and inspect only its encoder.
sessions.diagnostic: If direction and count signs disagree, stop and correct the documented direction setting before enabling feedback.
sessions.shortAction: With power disconnected, label the motor and encoder cable groups LEFT and RIGHT.
sessions.uncertainty: The expected count is based on a stated quadrature convention; the controller’s actual reporting must be measured.

sessions.title: Compare requested and measured wheel speed
sessions.why: A small speed trace shows whether the drivetrain follows requests before navigation depends on it.
needs: Verified encoder signs and zero command; exact tuning reference for the controller revision
Secure suspended wheels first, conservative motor/current settings and reachable disconnect
Floor tests require a clear bounded area with stairs blocked and people/pets outside
actions: Follow the documented velocity setup and configure justified limits for the actual motor and supply.
Record a small zero-to-low-speed-to-zero trace for one wheel with labelled numeric scales.
Repeat for the other wheel and inspect current, oscillation and return to zero.
sessions.finish: Both wheels follow small requests without sustained oscillation and return to zero within recorded operating limits.
sessions.artifact: Labelled speed traces or CSV exports, software versions and controller configuration
sessions.restart: Open the last labelled trace and identify which line is requested speed and which is measured speed.
sessions.diagnostic: If the trace oscillates or current rises, stop the run and check signs, tuning, drag and limits before adding load.
sessions.shortAction: Open a saved graph and label its signals, numeric axes and available time resolution.
sessions.uncertainty: Suspended-wheel response does not establish loaded floor behavior; record what each measured trial actually supports.

sessions.title: Get two ROS programs talking
sessions.why: A known ROS environment isolates later sensor and bridge faults from basic installation problems.
needs: Selected robot computer with native Ubuntu 24.04
Use ROS 2 Jazzy Desktop Install outside the model-training environment; keep motor outputs disabled
actions: Follow the Jazzy Ubuntu installation for the selected computer.
Source the same installation in two terminals and run talker and listener.
Save the OS, ROS and package versions and the commands that exchanged messages.
sessions.finish: Talker output has matching received messages in the second terminal.
sessions.artifact: Environment notes and the successful local message-exchange check
sessions.restart: Source Jazzy in two terminals and repeat the talker/listener exchange.
sessions.diagnostic: If nothing arrives, check both sourced installations and the Desktop demo packages before adding devices or networking.
sessions.shortAction: Record the Ubuntu release and verify which ROS installation the current shell uses.

reference.label: Install Jazzy and inspect a topic

sessions.uncertainty: Passing the local demo verifies this setup step; each real driver still needs its own compatibility and device check.

sessions.title: Give manual movement a bounded interface
sessions.why: Navigation needs a drive interface that rejects stale requests and reports measured movement.
needs: Verified wheel feedback, native Jazzy environment and measured geometry
Read the full interface contract; pinned driver candidate and local command-freshness guard
Suspended wheels first; floor tests remain supervised with blocked stairs and physical stop in reach
actions: Establish firmware and encoder queries with motor commands disabled.
Review or implement the contract for bounded commands, measured odometry, timeouts and deliberate re-arm.
Test loss of fresh commands while polling continues, bridge failure, network loss and physical stop; record the outcomes.
sessions.finish: Manual motion and every required stop/re-arm case have measured evidence; continued or resumed stale motion is resolved.
sessions.artifact: Pinned bridge revision, configuration, telemetry and command-age/stop test records
sessions.restart: Open the first unfinished contract row and reproduce its smallest read-only or wheels-supported check.
sessions.diagnostic: If polling keeps stale motion alive, locate the independent fresh-command-age check before attempting another floor run.
sessions.shortAction: With motor commands disabled, inspect the driver’s firmware/encoder query path and record its exact revision.

reference.label: Separate communication timeout from command freshness

sessions.uncertainty: The guide supplies an interface contract and driver candidate; a complete validated bridge and local freshness guard are implementation work.

sessions.title: See one real sensor measurement
sessions.why: An inspectable scan or image is the smallest useful proof that a real sensor is connected correctly.
needs: Verified native Jazzy setup, exact lidar/camera identity and matching driver
Motor outputs disabled; lidar stationary for the first view
Retain the chapter’s computer roles and topic/clock contract beside the device instructions
actions: Pin the matching driver and inspect its actual topic, type, frame, timestamp and rate.
Use the scan’s own frame for the first stationary RViz display and move a flat target a measured distance.
Save the device identity, configuration and screenshot; inspect the camera separately and keep depth optional.
sessions.finish: You can identify one real measurement and explain its units, frame, time and relation to the target you moved.
sessions.artifact: Device/version notes, lidar-bench.rviz and a labelled sensor screenshot
sessions.restart: Launch the known driver and reproduce the same stationary target view with outputs inhibited.
sessions.diagnostic: If RViz is blank while messages arrive, inspect display status, fixed frame and QoS before changing the driver.
sessions.shortAction: With outputs inhibited, record one device identity and its actual published topic/frame.
sessions.uncertainty: A viewer image does not establish depth; firmware, USB and ROS-driver support must be checked for each selected device.

sessions.title: Put measured coordinate arrows on the rover
sessions.why: Measured frames let a sensor observation become a meaningful location relative to the rover.
needs: Assembled chassis, fixed sensor mounts, ruler and frame sketch
Metres and radians in ROS; preserve the explicit conversion from CAD millimetres
actions: Mark the base_link origin projection and forward direction using the floor-plane convention.
Measure sensor position and orientation with units and the mount revision.
Draw map → odom → base_link → sensors and name one publisher for each relationship.
sessions.finish: You can locate the origin vertically and explain every measured offset and frame relationship.
sessions.artifact: Frame sketch, mount photograph and signed offsets with units
sessions.restart: Point to the real origin projection and compare one sensor offset with the sketch.
sessions.diagnostic: If an orientation is uncertain, use that exact sensor’s frame diagram before entering any rotation.
sessions.shortAction: Mark forward on the deck and measure one sensor’s offset in millimetres and metres.
sessions.uncertainty: A measured offset is incomplete without orientation; a changed mount revision requires revisiting the transform.

sessions.title: Compare wheel motion with a tape measure
sessions.why: A sign-and-scale check prevents a pretty room map from hiding incorrect wheel geometry.
needs: Verified manual drive/stop interface, encoder convention and frame sketch
Clear supervised floor, blocked stairs and reachable disconnect
For hand-roll logging, inhibit motor commands but keep controller/encoders powered; USB alone is insufficient
actions: Check forward count signs and positive left yaw with motor outputs inhibited.
Drive a measured short straight baseline slowly and compare tape travel with odometry.
Repeat before adjusting scale, then check a slow turn and save raw counts and geometry.
sessions.finish: Signs and short-run scale are credible, and raw measurements explain the comparison.
sessions.artifact: Counts, configured counts per revolution, wheel geometry and tape/odometry comparisons
sessions.restart: Open the last straight-line record and recover its units, signs and wheel parameters.
sessions.diagnostic: Resolve a wrong counting convention before tuning radius; investigate slip or loose hardware when errors are inconsistent.
sessions.shortAction: Recalculate one saved count-to-distance example using the recorded convention.

reference.label: Keep motion estimates in the intended frame

sessions.uncertainty: Wheel rotation estimates travel under an ideal rolling assumption; traction can make physical travel differ.

sessions.title: Mark what the lidar did and did not observe
sessions.why: Knowing the sensor’s blind spots prevents an unseen area from becoming an imagined safe route.
needs: Stationary live lidar, RViz and a broad cardboard target
Keep the test zone clear of low obstacles and physically isolated from stairs; depth remains optional
actions: Move the target a measured distance within the scan plane and inspect its returns.
Annotate observed surface, free ray and unknown space behind an obstruction.
Lift the target out of the scan plane and record what its disappearance does not establish.
sessions.finish: Your annotated observation distinguishes a surface, observed free ray and unknown space.
sessions.artifact: A labelled scan screenshot or sketch and the measured target movement
sessions.restart: Open the annotation and identify one area that is still unknown.
sessions.diagnostic: If a return disappears, first check the target’s height relative to the scan plane rather than marking the volume empty.
sessions.shortAction: Annotate one saved scan with a surface, a free ray and an unknown region.
sessions.uncertainty: A horizontal scan is a slice; it cannot establish clearance above/below the plane or detect every stair edge.

sessions.title: Check the live frame chain
sessions.why: A coherent live transform chain makes the upcoming recording interpretable instead of merely large.
needs: Running verified bridge and sensor publishers; measured frame sketch and wheel checks
Use one owner per transform and keep acquisition free of map → odom corrections
actions: Run the chapter’s frame and message inspection commands in sourced Jazzy.
Compare the live diagram with the measured sensor mounts and body convention.
Check frame ownership and timestamp availability, then save the diagram and any remaining mismatch.
sessions.finish: The live diagram agrees with physical frames and required sensor/odometry messages carry usable transforms.
sessions.artifact: Live frame diagram, topic checks and the matching mount revision
sessions.restart: Recreate the frame diagram and compare it with the saved physical sketch.
sessions.diagnostic: For jumps or missing transforms, check duplicate publishers and timestamps before increasing queues or tuning SLAM.
sessions.shortAction: Inspect one child frame and identify its sole parent and publisher.
sessions.uncertainty: The inspection commands do not create missing drivers or transforms; those publishers must already implement the measured contract.

sessions.title: Record one short room survey
sessions.why: A raw recording lets you improve mapping without repeatedly moving the robot around the room.
needs: Passing frame and manual-motion gates, working sensors and storage
One bounded room with stairs blocked, route clear of people/pets and physical stop within reach
Live clocks checked; SLAM, localization and navigation stopped; exclude motion-command topics
Keep Chapter 05’s recording topic/clock contract and the mapping prerequisite callout beside the acquisition steps
actions: Sketch a short loop and measure three observable reference spans in two directions.
Declare the provisional dimensional target and make a short stationary recording check.
Record the slow loop, inspect retained topics/transforms and save the acquisition manifest.
sessions.finish: One raw bag contains the planned route and required topics, with measurements and configuration recorded beside it.
sessions.artifact: data/room_001, run manifest, room sketch and three measured reference spans
sessions.restart: Read the bag summary and manifest before starting another acquisition.
sessions.diagnostic: If a stream is absent, inspect its actual name, QoS and rate and repeat a short sample before a whole-room run.
sessions.shortAction: Mark the exact endpoints and height of one reference span on the room sketch.

reference.label: Record and inspect a raw bag

sessions.uncertainty: The 0.10 m comparison target is a provisional course goal; only your survey measurements establish whether it is met.

sessions.title: Turn the recording into an inspectable map
sessions.why: Replaying the same observations makes a map problem a repeatable software experiment.
needs: Raw room bag, manifest and native Jazzy analysis environment
Motor power off and robot command processes stopped
Isolated replay ROS domain; no live publishers; matching replay clocks in every participating node
actions: Copy the installed SLAM Toolbox configuration and match its frame/topic names to the robot contract.
Run mapping and bag playback in the same isolated domain with simulated time.
Inspect map, scan and frames in RViz and compare the route with the room sketch.
sessions.finish: One replay produces an inspectable map with broadly consistent surfaces and a route you can compare with the sketch.
sessions.artifact: Mapping configuration, replay commands and an annotated first-map screenshot
sessions.restart: With motor power off, reopen the bag and the exact configuration that produced the saved view.
sessions.diagnostic: For a blank or doubled map, check names, clocks, transforms and old map corrections before tuning scan matching.
sessions.shortAction: Compare the configuration’s base, odom and map frame names with your saved frame diagram.

reference.label: SLAM Toolbox mapping and saved state

sessions.uncertainty: A consistent-looking image is a first inspection; independent dimensional checks come next.

sessions.title: Check the map against the room
sessions.why: Independent measurements turn the room picture into a bounded claim about layout accuracy.
needs: Inspectable map, raw bag and the three recorded physical reference spans
Use the same endpoints and height; note raster resolution and selected wall boundaries
actions: Measure the matching map spans and compute map minus physical distance.
Inspect the loop closure and compare each absolute error with the declared target.
Collect a second independent survey and repeat; if a target fails, record and investigate one justified cause.
sessions.finish: The three dimensional checks meet the declared acceptance target and a second independent survey supports the result. Keep failed attempts as evidence while correcting the map.
sessions.artifact: Signed-error table, map screenshots and second-survey comparison
sessions.restart: Recalculate one saved signed error from its physical and map distances.
sessions.diagnostic: If a span fails, replay the same bag after one justified correction; distinguish repeatable scale error from inconsistent data.
sessions.shortAction: Identify one physical reference span and its matching map endpoints.

reference.label: Inspect the mapping workflow and assumptions

sessions.uncertainty: Grid resolution is not measurement accuracy; endpoint selection and pose errors affect the result. Navigation needs a map fit for its tested route.

sessions.title: Save the map and its provenance
sessions.why: A versioned map package lets later navigation and observations refer to the same room coordinates.
needs: Running mapper in the isolated replay domain, checked map and measurement report
Retain the raw bag; keep map image and YAML metadata together
actions: Save the occupancy map using the same environment, domain and clock settings.
Save the mapping state as well if you intend to resume SLAM.
Package configuration, measurements, frame diagram and bag identity under a named map revision.
sessions.finish: The saved map has scale/origin metadata, a measurement report and a raw recording that can reproduce it.
sessions.artifact: Map YAML/image, map_revision and the provenance package
sessions.restart: Open the map YAML beside its image and confirm the matching revision and bag identifier.
sessions.diagnostic: If only a picture was saved, recover the scale/origin metadata before treating it as a navigation map.
sessions.shortAction: Write the map revision and list the raw bag and configuration that produced it.

reference.label: Save the occupancy map and mapping state

sessions.uncertainty: An occupancy raster and a serialized pose graph serve different purposes; retain the raw observations regardless.

sessions.title: Review the route from goal to motor
sessions.minutes: One or more 45–60 minute integration blocks
sessions.why: A reviewed robot contract makes navigation’s output traceable all the way to measured, stoppable motion.
needs: Saved map and measurement report, current mounts and verified manual stop tests
Actual Jazzy package versions and measured footprint, geometry and motion limits
One selected command source; retain blocked stairs and known physical clearance
Use the fixed-map AMCL route; SLAM and AMCL must not publish competing map corrections
actions: Recheck live transforms, sensor data and manual stop behavior at the current load.
Copy the installed Nav2 configuration and adapt each contract row from measured evidence.
Trace the final command type and route, freshness guards and local stopping behavior before enabling navigation.
sessions.finish: Every configuration row has a measured value or named tested implementation, including the command and failure routes.
sessions.artifact: Reviewed Nav2 configuration, version record and completed integration-contract notes
sessions.restart: Open the first unfinished contract row and identify the measurement or implementation it needs.
sessions.diagnostic: If the bridge or freshness guard is unfinished, complete that specific contract before an autonomous trial.
sessions.shortAction: With motor outputs inhibited, trace the configured final velocity topic to the bridge and record its message type.

reference.label: Integrate a custom robot with Nav2

sessions.uncertainty: The installed sample is not a calibrated rover configuration; adapting plugins and implementing guards are substantial integration work.

sessions.title: Place the stationary rover in its saved map
sessions.why: A plausible robot pose and responsive costmap are the evidence needed before sending a destination.
needs: Passing Nav2 configuration gate and verified live acquisition
Stop replay and SLAM; use the live ROS domain and a single map → odom owner
Motor outputs disabled initially; broad test obstacle visible in the scan plane
actions: Start the reviewed live stack and initialize AMCL to the real marked pose and heading.
Compare walls, footprint and map placement while stationary.
Add and remove the test obstacle and inspect marking, clearing and unknown space.
sessions.finish: Displayed placement agrees with reality, the footprint covers the rover and the obstacle appears and clears as expected.
sessions.artifact: Local/global costmap screenshots and a pose/obstacle inspection note
sessions.restart: With outputs inhibited, compare one real wall and the current heading with the saved map view.
sessions.diagnostic: If walls disagree, check initialization, map revision, transforms and timing before changing planner parameters.
sessions.shortAction: Verify the loaded map revision and identify the current map → odom publisher with outputs inhibited.
sessions.uncertainty: Loading a map does not tell the rover where it was placed; localization and obstacle updates need direct checks.

sessions.title: Make one short measured trip
sessions.why: A half-metre trip gives the first autonomous movement a visible destination and a physical success check.
needs: Passing localization/costmap gate and proven local stop behavior
Clear supervised route, blocked stairs, people/pets outside and stop within reach
Use demonstrated low speed and review recovery maneuvers before enabling motion
actions: Mark a destination about half a metre ahead and inspect the entire planned swept footprint.
Run the short goal through the verified command route and observe physical motion and status.
Measure the final error and stopping, then save three trials including unsuccessful attempts.
sessions.finish: Three trial records show repeatable short-route behavior, measured endpoints and dependable stopping.
sessions.artifact: Waypoint-trial log with endpoint error, timing, outcome and any intervention
sessions.restart: Read the last trial’s start mark, map revision, limits and intervention before repeating it.
sessions.diagnostic: If the rover oscillates near the goal, inspect controllable speed and odometry before goal tolerance and controller limits.
sessions.shortAction: With motion disabled, mark the goal and inspect the planned footprint along the short route.
sessions.uncertainty: The initial 0.15 m endpoint target is provisional; a success status alone does not establish physical arrival or stopped wheels.

sessions.title: Test when the rover should stop or refuse
sessions.minutes: About 45–60 minutes per group of checks
sessions.why: A useful home rover needs a measured response to changes and missing information.
needs: Repeatable short trip, broad scan-plane obstacle and supervised bounded floor
Reachable stop and blocked stairs; test required-sensor loss with outputs disabled first
actions: Block the route with the visible obstacle and inspect a clearance-respecting alternate path or refusal.
Test cancellation and fresh-command loss, recording delay and travel after the request.
Check sensor-freshness inhibition, restore normal conditions and repeat the uncomplicated trip.
sessions.finish: The log shows obstacle handling/refusal and tested cancellation, timeout and sensor-loss behavior with a recovery procedure.
sessions.artifact: Failure-test records and the floor/load/speed/sensor envelope that passed
sessions.restart: Open the failure-test log and identify the next unverified case and its disabled-output first check.
sessions.diagnostic: If a guard fails, keep motion inhibited and inspect the specific freshness/stop path before another moving trial.
sessions.shortAction: With outputs disabled, interrupt one required stream and inspect whether the freshness guard inhibits motion.

reference.label: Make failure behavior part of integration

sessions.uncertainty: Passing a broad obstacle test does not establish detection of low toys, shoelaces, glass or stair edges.

sessions.title: Query the supplied observation example
sessions.why: A small inspectable example teaches what an observation can support before we join your real robot data.
needs: The Chapter 03 Python environment, memory.py, demo records and data contract
Keep the illustrative demo database separate from future real observations
actions: Import the supplied records and reproduce the stated historical query.
Change the time window, score filter and map revision and explain which evidence remains.
Import the unchanged data again and inspect the distinction between candidates and all recent observations.
sessions.finish: You can explain inclusion/exclusion, deduplication and why the demo establishes no current object position.
sessions.artifact: memory/demo.sqlite, original demo records and annotated query output
sessions.restart: Run the known historical query against the unchanged demo and inspect its first returned record.
sessions.diagnostic: If import fails, check one complete JSON object per line and timezone-bearing timestamps using the untouched demo first.
sessions.shortAction: Inspect one demo record and point to its image reference, time, map revision and null object position.

reference.label: Keep scores distinct from established probabilities

sessions.uncertainty: The demo image paths and poses are illustrative; completing it does not complete the real-observation milestone.

sessions.title: Connect five real predictions to the room
sessions.why: This is where the rover you built and the model you trained become one inspectable household-observation system.
needs: Saved evaluated model, mounted camera, checked map and frame measurements
Read the shared memory contract for label/score conversion and provenance
Stationary marked base_link poses with documented uncertainty; motor outputs inhibited
actions: Mark two measured rover poses in the current map and capture five distinct present/absent images with actual times.
Run the saved model and build five records using real identifiers, documented observer poses and null object positions.
Import into a separate real database and query all five; open every image and inspect its decision and capture-pose evidence.
sessions.finish: Five real records appear in recent_observations and each image, model identity, capture time and observer pose can be checked.
sessions.artifact: memory/observations-own.jsonl, memory/own.sqlite, five real images and pose-measurement notes
sessions.restart: Open one referenced image and trace its record back to the saved model and physically marked capture pose.
sessions.diagnostic: If a pose lacks evidence, leave it out of the real database and finish the frame/map check; preserve incorrect predictions honestly.
sessions.shortAction: Prepare one actual image and model output, or inspect one record’s label/score conversion without inventing missing poses.

reference.label: Keep observer pose and object position distinct

sessions.uncertainty: The starter stores references but cannot verify image existence or pose accuracy; your inspection supplies that evidence. Automatic ROS association is later work.

sessions.title: Transform a measured point on paper
sessions.why: A small geometry calculation shows what additional evidence a future object location will require.
needs: Paper, calculator and the established base/map frame conventions
Treat the worked numbers as illustrative; an image-only prediction has no measured depth
actions: Draw the supplied measured base-frame point at zero yaw and at a quarter-turn.
Apply the planar transform and compare it with the drawing.
Name the missing intrinsics, depth and time-matched transforms for a real camera pixel.
sessions.finish: The arithmetic and sketch agree, and observer pose, measured object point and image-only prediction stay distinct.
sessions.artifact: Annotated two-pose calculation and a list of missing localization inputs
sessions.restart: Recalculate the zero-yaw example and identify which measurements its formula assumes.
sessions.diagnostic: If signs disagree, draw forward/left axes at both headings and check the rotation before using software.
sessions.shortAction: Draw the zero-yaw example and predict the quarter-turn result.
sessions.uncertainty: This is an optional paper exercise; the current observation schema intentionally rejects object coordinates until a new localization contract is designed.
